title: ledger.json
description: Every figure the deck states, recorded once, at full scale, with the verbatim string it was read from. `raw` and `value` are two independent statements about the same number and ledger.py refuses the ledger when they disagree — that disagreement is the whole scale-error class, caught without seeing the deck.

id.description: Stable within the ledger; relations address figures by it.

value.description: The number at FULL scale. A slide reading "$493K" is 493000 here, never 493.

raw.description: The slide's own string, verbatim: "$493K", "~55%", "18-24 months". Scale, approximation markers and ranges are all read back off this.

label.description: What the figure is, in the deck's own words where possible.

quote.description: The verbatim sentence or table row the figure was read from. This is what the second read is checked against, so a paraphrase defeats the gate. It must keep the words that say what the number is — "Net revenue $493K", not "$493K": the check matches text, so a quote of nothing but the figure is re-found on any slide that prints that figure and confirms nothing. A quote carrying no word warns.

currency.description: ISO code. Required in practice for money: a relation across two currencies is refused, not converted.

period.description: The time basis a rate is quoted over — "month", "year". A monthly figure summed against an annual one is refused.
